## [Objectives]{.HTitleText1} {#h-1004151 .Part}

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Objectives

**[[1]{.sectionLabel}]{#
                            s-1 .sectionLabel}** The objectives of these
Guidelines are

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} to establish a fair standard of support for children
  that ensures that they continue to benefit from the financial means of
  both spouses after separation;

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} to reduce conflict and tension between spouses by
  making the calculation of child support orders more objective;

- [(c)]{.lawlabel} to improve the efficiency of the legal process by
  giving courts and spouses guidance in setting the levels of child
  support orders and encouraging settlement; and

- [(d)]{.lawlabel} to ensure consistent treatment of spouses and
  children who are in similar circumstances.

## [Interpretation]{.HTitleText1} {#h-1004158 .Part}

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Definitions

- **[[2]{.sectionLabel}]{#
                              s-2 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} The
  definitions in this subsection apply in these Guidelines.

  [[Act]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

  :   [[Act]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means the [Divorce
      Act](/eng/acts/D-3.4). ([Loi]{.DefinedTermLink lang="fr"})

  [[child]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

  :   [[child]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means a child of the
      marriage. ([enfant]{.DefinedTermLink lang="fr"})

  [[income]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

  :   [[income]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means the annual income determined
      under sections 15 to 20. ([revenu]{.DefinedTermLink lang="fr"})

  [[majority of parenting time]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

  :   [[majority of parenting time]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means a period
      of time that is more than 60% of parenting time over the course of
      a year. ([majorité du temps parental]{.DefinedTermLink lang="fr"})

  [[order assignee]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

  :   [[order assignee]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means a minister, member or
      agency referred to in subsection 20.1(1) of the Act to whom a
      child support order is assigned in accordance with that
      subsection. ([cessionnaire de la créance
      alimentaire]{.DefinedTermLink lang="fr"})

  [[spouse]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

  :   [[spouse]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}[\[Repealed, SOR/2020-247, s.
      1\]]{.Repealed}

  [[table]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

  :   [[table]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means a federal child support table
      set out in Schedule I. ([table]{.DefinedTermLink lang="fr"})

  [[universal child care benefit]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

  :   [[universal child care benefit]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means a
      benefit provided under section 4 of the Universal Child Care
      Benefit Act. ([prestation universelle pour la garde
      d'enfants]{.DefinedTermLink lang="fr"})

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}[Income Tax Act](/eng/acts/I-3.3)

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} Words and expressions that are used in sections 15 to
  21 and that are not defined in this section have the meanings assigned
  to them under the [Income Tax Act](/eng/acts/I-3.3).

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Most current information

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} Where, for the purposes of these Guidelines, any
  amount is determined on the basis of specified information, the most
  current information must be used.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Application of Guidelines

  [(4)]{.lawlabel} In addition to child support orders, these Guidelines
  apply, with such modifications as the circumstances require, to

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} interim orders under subsections 15.1(2), 18.1(12)
    or 19(10) of the Act;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} orders varying a child support order;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} orders under subsections 18.1(15), 19(13), 28.5(5)
    or 29.1(5) of the Act;

  - [(c.1)]{.lawlabel} calculations of child support under subsection
    25.01(1) of the Act; and

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} recalculations of the amount of child support
    orders under subsection 25.1(1) of the Act.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Calculations and recalculations

  [(5)]{.lawlabel} For greater certainty, the provisions of these
  Guidelines that confer a discretionary power on a court do not apply
  to calculations or recalculations by a provincial child support
  service under subsection 25.01(1) or 25.1(1) of the Act.

## [Amount of Child Support]{.HTitleText1} {#h-1004183 .Part}

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Presumptive rule

- **[[3]{.sectionLabel}]{#
                              s-3
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Unless otherwise provided under
  these Guidelines, the amount of a child support order for children
  under the age of majority is

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the amount set out in the applicable table,
    according to the number of children under the age of majority to
    whom the order relates and the income of the spouse against whom the
    order is sought; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the amount, if any, determined under section 7.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Child the age of majority or over

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} Unless otherwise provided under these Guidelines,
  where a child to whom a child support order relates is the age of
  majority or over, the amount of the child support order is

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the amount determined by applying these Guidelines
    as if the child were under the age of majority; or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} if the court considers that approach to be
    inappropriate, the amount that it considers appropriate, having
    regard to the condition, means, needs and other circumstances of the
    child and the financial ability of each spouse to contribute to the
    support of the child.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Applicable table

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} The applicable table is

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} if the spouse against whom an order is sought
    resides in Canada,

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} the table for the province in which that spouse
      habitually resides at the time the application for the child
      support order or for a variation order in respect of the child
      support order is made,

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} if the court is satisfied that the province in
      which that spouse habitually resides has changed since the time
      described in subparagraph (i), the table for the province in which
      the spouse habitually resides at the time of determining the
      amount of support, or

    - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} if the court is satisfied that, in the near
      future after determination of the amount of support, that spouse
      will habitually reside in a given province other than the province
      in which the spouse habitually resides at the time of that
      determination, the table for the given province;

  - [(a.1)]{.lawlabel} if the spouse who is subject to a calculation or
    recalculation under subsection 25.01(1) or 25.1(1) of the Act
    resides in Canada, the table for the province in which that spouse
    habitually resides at the time the amount of child support is to be
    calculated or recalculated under subsection 25.01(1) or 25.1(1) of
    the Act; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} if the spouse against whom a child support order is
    sought, or who is subject to a calculation or a recalculation under
    subsection 25.01(1) or 25.1(1) of the Act, resides outside of
    Canada, or if the residence of that spouse is unknown, the table for
    the province where the other spouse habitually resides at the time
    the application for the child support order or for a variation order
    in respect of the child support order is made, or at the time the
    amount of child support is to be calculated or recalculated under
    subsection 25.01(1) or 25.1(1) of the Act.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/97-563, s. 1
- [SOR/2020-247, s. 2](#1274804-1286008){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1274804-1286008.html"}
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-3-20060322.html "Link to previous version of section 3"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Incomes over \$150,000

**[[4]{.sectionLabel}]{#
                            s-4 .sectionLabel}** Where the income of the
spouse against whom a child support order is sought is over \$150,000,
the amount of a child support order is

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} the amount determined under section 3; or

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} if the court considers that amount to be
  inappropriate,

  - [(i)]{.lawlabel} in respect of the first \$150,000 of the spouse's
    income, the amount set out in the applicable table for the number of
    children under the age of majority to whom the order relates;

  - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} in respect of the balance of the spouse's income,
    the amount that the court considers appropriate, having regard to
    the condition, means, needs and other circumstances of the children
    who are entitled to support and the financial ability of each spouse
    to contribute to the support of the children; and

  - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} the amount, if any, determined under section 7.

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Spouse in place of a parent

**[[5]{.sectionLabel}]{#
                            s-5 .sectionLabel}** Where the spouse
against whom a child support order is sought stands in the place of a
parent for a child, the amount of a child support order is, in respect
of that spouse, such amount as the court considers appropriate, having
regard to these Guidelines and any other parent's legal duty to support
the child.

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Medical and dental insurance

**[[6]{.sectionLabel}]{#
                            s-6 .sectionLabel}** In making a child
support order, where medical or dental insurance coverage for the child
is available to either spouse through his or her employer or otherwise
at a reasonable rate, the court may order that coverage be acquired or
continued.

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Special or extraordinary expenses

- **[[7]{.sectionLabel}]{#
                              s-7 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} In a
  child support order the court may, on either spouse's request, provide
  for an amount to cover all or any portion of the following expenses,
  which expenses may be estimated, taking into account the necessity of
  the expense in relation to the child's best interests and the
  reasonableness of the expense in relation to the means of the spouses
  and those of the child and to the family's spending pattern prior to
  the separation:

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} child care expenses incurred as a result of the
    employment, illness, disability or education or training for
    employment of the spouse who has the majority of parenting time;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} that portion of the medical and dental insurance
    premiums attributable to the child;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} health-related expenses that exceed insurance
    reimbursement by at least \$100 annually, including orthodontic
    treatment, professional counselling provided by a psychologist,
    social worker, psychiatrist or any other person, physiotherapy,
    occupational therapy, speech therapy and prescription drugs, hearing
    aids, glasses and contact lenses;

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} extraordinary expenses for primary or secondary
    school education or for any other educational programs that meet the
    child's particular needs;

  - [(e)]{.lawlabel} expenses for post-secondary education; and

  - [(f)]{.lawlabel} extraordinary expenses for extracurricular
    activities.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Definition of "extraordinary expenses"

  [(1.1)]{.lawlabel} For the purposes of paragraphs (1)(d) and (f), the
  term [[extraordinary expenses]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} expenses that exceed those that the spouse
    requesting an amount for the extraordinary expenses can reasonably
    cover, taking into account that spouse's income and the amount that
    the spouse would receive under the applicable table or, where the
    court has determined that the table amount is inappropriate, the
    amount that the court has otherwise determined is appropriate; or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} where paragraph (a) is not applicable, expenses
    that the court considers are extraordinary taking into account

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} the amount of the expense in relation to the
      income of the spouse requesting the amount, including the amount
      that the spouse would receive under the applicable table or, where
      the court has determined that the table amount is inappropriate,
      the amount that the court has otherwise determined is appropriate,

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} the nature and number of the educational
      programs and extracurricular activities,

    - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} any special needs and talents of the child or
      children,

    - [(iv)]{.lawlabel} the overall cost of the programs and activities,
      and

    - [(v)]{.lawlabel} any other similar factor that the court considers
      relevant.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Sharing of expense

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} The guiding principle in determining the amount of an
  expense referred to in subsection (1) is that the expense is shared by
  the spouses in proportion to their respective incomes after deducting
  from the expense, the contribution, if any, from the child.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Subsidies, tax deductions, etc.

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} Subject to subsection (4), in determining the amount
  of an expense referred to in subsection (1), the court must take into
  account any subsidies, benefits or income tax deductions or credits
  relating to the expense, and any eligibility to claim a subsidy,
  benefit or income tax deduction or credit relating to the expense.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Universal child care benefit

  [(4)]{.lawlabel} In determining the amount of an expense referred to
  in subsection (1), the court shall not take into account any universal
  child care benefit or any eligibility to claim that benefit.

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Split parenting time

**[[8]{.sectionLabel}]{#
                            s-8 .sectionLabel}** If there are two or
more children, and each spouse has the majority of parenting time with
one or more of those children, the amount of a child support order is
the difference between the amount that each spouse would otherwise pay
if a child support order were sought against each of the spouses.

::: HistoricalNote
- [SOR/2020-247, s. 4](#1274813-1286035){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1274813-1286035.html"}
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-8-20060322.html "Link to previous version of section 8"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Shared parenting time

**[[9]{.sectionLabel}]{#
                            s-9 .sectionLabel}** If each spouse
exercises not less than 40% of parenting time with a child over the
course of a year, the amount of the child support order must be
determined by taking into account

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} the amounts set out in the applicable tables for each
  of the spouses;

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} the increased costs of shared parenting time
  arrangements; and

- [(c)]{.lawlabel} the conditions, means, needs and other circumstances
  of each spouse and of any child for whom support is sought.

::: HistoricalNote
- [SOR/2020-247, s. 5](#1274815-1286040){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1274815-1286040.html"}
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-9-20060322.html "Link to previous version of section 9"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Undue hardship

- **[[10]{.sectionLabel}]{#
                              s-10 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} On
  either spouse's application, a court may award an amount of child
  support that is different from the amount determined under any of
  sections 3 to 5, 8 or 9 if the court finds that the spouse making the
  request, or a child in respect of whom the request is made, would
  otherwise suffer undue hardship.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Circumstances that may cause undue
  hardship

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} Circumstances that may cause a spouse or child to
  suffer undue hardship include the following:

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the spouse has responsibility for an unusually high
    level of debts reasonably incurred to support the spouses and their
    children prior to the separation or to earn a living;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the spouse has unusually high expenses in relation
    to exercising parenting time with a child;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} the spouse has a legal duty under a judgment, order
    or written separation agreement to support any person;

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} the spouse has a legal duty to support a child,
    other than a child of the marriage, who is

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} under the age of majority, or

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} the age of majority or over but is unable, by
      reason of illness, disability or other cause, to obtain the
      necessaries of life; and

  - [(e)]{.lawlabel} the spouse has a legal duty to support any person
    who is unable to obtain the necessaries of life due to an illness or
    disability.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Standards of living must be considered

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} Despite a determination of undue hardship under
  subsection (1), an application under that subsection must be denied by
  the court if it is of the opinion that the household of the spouse who
  claims undue hardship would, after determining the amount of child
  support under any of sections 3 to 5, 8 or 9, have a higher standard
  of living than the household of the other spouse.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Standards of living test

  [(4)]{.lawlabel} In comparing standards of living for the purpose of
  subsection (3), the court may use the comparison of household
  standards of living test set out in Schedule II.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Reasonable time

  [(5)]{.lawlabel} Where the court awards a different amount of child
  support under subsection (1), it may specify, in the child support
  order, a reasonable time for the satisfaction of any obligation
  arising from circumstances that cause undue hardship and the amount
  payable at the end of that time.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Reasons

  [(6)]{.lawlabel} Where the court makes a child support order in a
  different amount under this section, it must record its reasons for
  doing so.

::: HistoricalNote
- [SOR/2020-247, s. 6](#1274820-1286044){.wb-lbx

## [Elements of a Child Support Order]{.HTitleText1} {#h-1004266 .Part}

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Form of payments

**[[11]{.sectionLabel}]{#
                            s-11 .sectionLabel}** The court may require
in a child support order that the amount payable under the order be paid
in periodic payments, in a lump sum or in a lump sum and periodic
payments.

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Security

**[[12]{.sectionLabel}]{#
                            s-12 .sectionLabel}** The court may require
in the child support order that the amount payable under the order be
paid or secured, or paid and secured, in the manner specified in the
order.

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Information to be specified in order

**[[13]{.sectionLabel}]{#
                            s-13 .sectionLabel}** A child support order
must include the following information:

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} the name and birth date of each child to whom the
  order relates;

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} the income of any spouse whose income is used to
  determine the amount of the child support order;

- [(c)]{.lawlabel} the amount determined under paragraph 3(1)(a) for the
  number of children to whom the order relates;

- [(d)]{.lawlabel} the amount determined under paragraph 3(2)(b) for a
  child the age of majority or over;

- [(e)]{.lawlabel} the particulars of any expense described in
  subsection 7(1), the child to whom the expense relates, and the amount
  of the expense or, where that amount cannot be determined, the
  proportion to be paid in relation to the expense; and

- [(f)]{.lawlabel} the date on which the lump sum or first payment is
  payable and the day of the month or other time period on which all
  subsequent payments are to be made.

## [Variation of Child Support Orders]{.HTitleText1} {#h-1004279 .Part}

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Circumstances for variation

**[[14]{.sectionLabel}]{#
                            s-14 .sectionLabel}** For the purposes of
subsection 17(4) of the Act, any one of the following constitutes a
change of circumstances that gives rise to the making of a variation
order in respect of a child support order:

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} in the case where the amount of child support
  includes a determination made in accordance with the applicable table,
  any change in circumstances that would result in a different child
  support order or any provision thereof;

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} in the case where the amount of child support does
  not include a determination made in accordance with a table, any
  change in the condition, means, needs or other circumstances of either
  spouse or of any child who is entitled to support; and

- [(c)]{.lawlabel} in the case of an order made before May 1, 1997, the
  coming into force of section 15.1 of the Act, enacted by section 2 of
  chapter 1 of the Statutes of Canada, (1997).

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/97-563, s. 2
- SOR/2000-337, s. 2
:::

## [Income]{.HTitleText1} {#h-1004287 .Part}

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Determination of annual income

- **[[15]{.sectionLabel}]{#
                              s-15
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Subject to subsection (2), a
  spouse's annual income is determined by the court in accordance with
  sections 16 to 20.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Agreement

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} Where both spouses agree in writing on the annual
  income of a spouse, the court may consider that amount to be the
  spouse's income for the purposes of these Guidelines if the court
  thinks that the amount is reasonable having regard to the income
  information provided under section 21.

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Calculation of annual income

**[[16]{.sectionLabel}]{#
                            s-16 .sectionLabel}** Subject to sections 17
to 20, a spouse's annual income is determined using the sources of
income set out under the heading "Total income" in the T1 General form
issued by the Canada Revenue Agency and is adjusted in accordance with
Schedule III.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2000-337, s. 3
- SOR/2007-59, s. 4
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-16-20060322.html "Link to previous version of section 16"){.PITLink}
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Pattern of income

- **[[17]{.sectionLabel}]{#
                              s-17 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} If
  the court is of the opinion that the determination of a spouse's
  annual income under section 16 would not be the fairest determination
  of that income, the court may have regard to the spouse's income over
  the last three years and determine an amount that is fair and
  reasonable in light of any pattern of income, fluctuation in income or
  receipt of a non-recurring amount during those years.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Non-recurring losses

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} Where a spouse has incurred a non-recurring capital
  or business investment loss, the court may, if it is of the opinion
  that the determination of the spouse's annual income under section 16
  would not provide the fairest determination of the annual income,
  choose not to apply sections 6 and 7 of Schedule III, and adjust the
  amount of the loss, including related expenses and carrying charges
  and interest expenses, to arrive at such amount as the court considers
  appropriate.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2000-337, s. 4
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Shareholder, director or officer

- **[[18]{.sectionLabel}]{#
                              s-18
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Where a spouse is a shareholder,
  director or officer of a corporation and the court is of the opinion
  that the amount of the spouse's annual income as determined under
  section 16 does not fairly reflect all the money available to the
  spouse for the payment of child support, the court may consider the
  situations described in section 17 and determine the spouse's annual
  income to include

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} all or part of the pre-tax income of the
    corporation, and of any corporation that is related to that
    corporation, for the most recent taxation year; or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} an amount commensurate with the services that the
    spouse provides to the corporation, provided that the amount does
    not exceed the corporation's pre-tax income.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Adjustment to corporation's pre-tax
  income

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} In determining the pre-tax income of a corporation
  for the purposes of subsection (1), all amounts paid by the
  corporation as salaries, wages or management fees, or other payments
  or benefits, to or on behalf of persons with whom the corporation does
  not deal at arm's length must be added to the pre-tax income, unless
  the spouse establishes that the payments were reasonable in the
  circumstances.

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Imputing income

- **[[19]{.sectionLabel}]{#
                              s-19 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} The
  court may impute such amount of income to a spouse as it considers
  appropriate in the circumstances, which circumstances include the
  following:

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the spouse is intentionally under-employed or
    unemployed, other than where the under-employment or unemployment is
    required by the needs of a child of the marriage or any child under
    the age of majority or by the reasonable educational or health needs
    of the spouse;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the spouse is exempt from paying federal or
    provincial income tax;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} the spouse lives in a country that has effective
    rates of income tax that are significantly lower than those in
    Canada;

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} it appears that income has been diverted which
    would affect the level of child support to be determined under these
    Guidelines;

  - [(e)]{.lawlabel} the spouse's property is not reasonably utilized to
    generate income;

  - [(f)]{.lawlabel} the spouse has failed to provide income information
    when under a legal obligation to do so;

  - [(g)]{.lawlabel} the spouse unreasonably deducts expenses from
    income;

  - [(h)]{.lawlabel} the spouse derives a significant portion of income
    from dividends, capital gains or other sources that are taxed at a
    lower rate than employment or business income or that are exempt
    from tax; and

  - [(i)]{.lawlabel} the spouse is a beneficiary under a trust and is or
    will be in receipt of income or other benefits from the trust.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Reasonableness of expenses

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} For the purpose of paragraph (1)(g), the
  reasonableness of an expense deduction is not solely governed by
  whether the deduction is permitted under the [Income Tax
  Act](/eng/acts/I-3.3).

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2000-337, s. 5
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Non-resident

- **[[20]{.sectionLabel}]{#
                              s-20
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Subject to subsection (2), where a
  spouse is a non-resident of Canada, the spouse's annual income is
  determined as though the spouse were a resident of Canada.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Non-resident taxed at higher rates

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} If a spouse is a non-resident of Canada and resides
  in a country that has effective rates of income tax that are
  significantly higher than those applicable in the province in which
  the other spouse habitually resides, the spouse's annual income is the
  amount that the court determines to be appropriate taking those rates
  into consideration.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2005-400, s. 2
- [SOR/2020-247, s. 7(E)](#1274822-1286047){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1274822-1286047.html"}
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-20-20060501.html "Link to previous version of section 20"){.PITLink}
:::

## [Income Information]{.HTitleText1} {#h-1004334 .Part}

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Obligation of applicant

- **[[21]{.sectionLabel}]{#
                              s-21 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} A
  spouse who is applying for a child support order and whose income
  information is necessary to determine the amount of the order must
  include the following with the application:

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} a copy of every personal income tax return filed by
    the spouse for each of the three most recent taxation years;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} a copy of every notice of assessment and
    reassessment issued to the spouse for each of the three most recent
    taxation years;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} where the spouse is an employee, the most recent
    statement of earnings indicating the total earnings paid in the year
    to date, including overtime or, where such a statement is not
    provided by the employer, a letter from the spouse's employer
    setting out that information including the spouse's rate of annual
    salary or remuneration;

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} where the spouse is self-employed, for the three
    most recent taxation years

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} the financial statements of the spouse's business
      or professional practice, other than a partnership, and

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} a statement showing a breakdown of all salaries,
      wages, management fees or other payments or benefits paid to, or
      on behalf of, persons or corporations with whom the spouse does
      not deal at arm's length;

  - [(e)]{.lawlabel} where the spouse is a partner in a partnership,
    confirmation of the spouse's income and draw from, and capital in,
    the partnership for its three most recent taxation years;

  - [(f)]{.lawlabel} where the spouse controls a corporation, for its
    three most recent taxation years

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} the financial statements of the corporation and
      its subsidiaries, and

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} a statement showing a breakdown of all salaries,
      wages, management fees or other payments or benefits paid to, or
      on behalf of, persons or corporations with whom the corporation,
      and every related corporation, does not deal at arm's length;

  - [(g)]{.lawlabel} where the spouse is a beneficiary under a trust, a
    copy of the trust settlement agreement and copies of the trust's
    three most recent financial statements; and

  - [(h)]{.lawlabel} in addition to any income information that must be
    included under paragraphs (c) to (g), where the spouse receives
    income from employment insurance, social assistance, a pension,
    workers compensation, disability payments or any other source, the
    most recent statement of income indicating the total amount of
    income from the applicable source during the current year, or if
    such a statement is not provided, a letter from the appropriate
    authority stating the required information.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Obligation of respondent

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} A spouse who is served with an application for a
  child support order and whose income information is necessary to
  determine the amount of the order, must, within 30 days after the
  application is served if the spouse resides in Canada or the United
  States or within 60 days if the spouse resides elsewhere, or such
  other time limit as the court specifies, provide the court, as well as
  the other spouse or the order assignee, as the case may be, with the
  documents referred to in subsection (1).

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Special expenses or undue hardship

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} Where, in the course of proceedings in respect of an
  application for a child support order, a spouse requests an amount to
  cover expenses referred to in subsection 7(1) or pleads undue
  hardship, the spouse who would be receiving the amount of child
  support must, within 30 days after the amount is sought or undue
  hardship is pleaded if the spouse resides in Canada or the United
  States or within 60 days if the spouse resides elsewhere, or such
  other time limit as the court specifies, provide the court and the
  other spouse with the documents referred to in subsection (1).

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Income over \$150,000

  [(4)]{.lawlabel} Where, in the course of proceedings in respect of an
  application for a child support order, it is established that the
  income of the spouse who would be paying the amount of child support
  is greater than \$150,000, the other spouse must, within 30 days after
  the income is established to be greater than \$150,000 if the other
  spouse resides in Canada or the United States or within 60 days if the
  other spouse resides elsewhere, or such other time limit as the court
  specifies, provide the court and the spouse with the documents
  referred to in subsection (1).

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Making of rules not precluded

  [(5)]{.lawlabel} Nothing in this section precludes the making of rules
  by a competent authority, within the meaning of section 25 of the Act,
  respecting the disclosure of income information that is considered
  necessary for the purposes of the determination of an amount of a
  child support order.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2000-337, s. 6
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Failure to comply

- **[[22]{.sectionLabel}]{#
                              s-22
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Where a spouse fails to comply with
  section 21, the other spouse may apply

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} to have the application for a child support order
    set down for a hearing, or move for judgment; or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} for an order requiring the spouse who failed to
    comply to provide the court, as well as the other spouse or order
    assignee, as the case may be, with the required documents.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Costs of the proceedings

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} Where a court makes an order under paragraph (1)(a)
  or (b), the court may award costs in favour of the other spouse up to
  an amount that fully compensates the other spouse for all costs
  incurred in the proceedings.

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Adverse inference

**[[23]{.sectionLabel}]{#
                            s-23 .sectionLabel}** Where the court
proceeds to a hearing on the basis of an application under paragraph
22(1)(a), the court may draw an adverse inference against the spouse who
failed to comply and impute income to that spouse in such amount as it
considers appropriate.

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Failure to comply with court order

**[[24]{.sectionLabel}]{#
                            s-24 .sectionLabel}** Where a spouse fails
to comply with an order issued on the basis of an application under
paragraph 22(1)(b), the court may

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} strike out any of the spouse's pleadings;

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} make a contempt order against the spouse;

- [(c)]{.lawlabel} proceed to a hearing, in the course of which it may
  draw an adverse inference against the spouse and impute income to that
  spouse in such amount as it considers appropriate; and

- [(d)]{.lawlabel} award costs in favour of the other spouse up to an
  amount that fully compensates the other spouse for all costs incurred
  in the proceedings.

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Continuing obligation to provide income
information

- **[[25]{.sectionLabel}]{#
                              s-25
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Every spouse against whom a child
  support order has been made must, on the written request of the other
  spouse or the order assignee, not more than once a year after the
  making of the order and as long as the child is a child within the
  meaning of these Guidelines, provide that other spouse or the order
  assignee with

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the documents referred to in subsection 21(1) for
    any of the three most recent taxation years for which the spouse has
    not previously provided the documents;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} as applicable, any current information, in writing,
    about the status of any expenses included in the order pursuant to
    subsection 7(1); and

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} as applicable, any current information, in writing,
    about the circumstances relied on by the court in a determination of
    undue hardship.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Below minimum income

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} Where a court has determined that the spouse against
  whom a child support order is sought does not have to pay child
  support because his or her income level is below the minimum amount
  required for application of the tables, that spouse must, on the
  written request of the other spouse, not more than once a year after
  the determination and as long as the child is a child within the
  meaning of these Guidelines, provide the other spouse with the
  documents referred to in subsection 21(1) for any of the three most
  recent taxation years for which the spouse has not previously provided
  the documents.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Obligation of receiving spouse

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} Where the income information of the spouse in favour
  of whom a child support order is made is used to determine the amount
  of the order, the spouse must, not more than once a year after the
  making of the order and as long as the child is a child within the
  meaning of these Guidelines, on the written request of the other
  spouse, provide the other spouse with the documents and information
  referred to in subsection (1).

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Information requests

  [(4)]{.lawlabel} Where a spouse or an order assignee requests
  information from the other spouse under any of subsections (1) to (3)
  and the income information of the requesting spouse is used to
  determine the amount of the child support order, the requesting spouse
  or order assignee must include the documents and information referred
  to in subsection (1) with the request.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Time limit

  [(5)]{.lawlabel} A spouse who receives a request made under any of
  subsections (1) to (3) must provide the required documents within 30
  days after the request's receipt if the spouse resides in Canada or
  the United States and within 60 days after the request's receipt if
  the spouse resides elsewhere.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Deemed receipt

  [(6)]{.lawlabel} A request made under any of subsections (1) to (3) is
  deemed to have been received 10 days after it is sent.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Failure to comply

  [(7)]{.lawlabel} A court may, on application by either spouse or an
  order assignee, where the other spouse has failed to comply with any
  of subsections (1) to (3)

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} consider the other spouse to be in contempt of
    court and award costs in favour of the applicant up to an amount
    that fully compensates the applicant for all costs incurred in the
    proceedings; or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} make an order requiring the other spouse to provide
    the required documents to the court, as well as to the spouse or
    order assignee, as the case may be.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Unenforceable provision

  [(8)]{.lawlabel} A provision in a judgment, order or agreement
  purporting to limit a spouse's obligation to provide documents under
  this section is unenforceable.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/97-563, s. 3(E)
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Provincial child support service

**[[26]{.sectionLabel}]{#
                            s-26 .sectionLabel}** For the purposes of
the recalculation of child support under subsection 25.1(1) of the Act,
a spouse or an order assignee may appoint a provincial child support
service to act on their behalf for the purposes of requesting and
receiving income information under any of subsections 25(1) to (3), as
well as for the purposes of an application under subsection 25(7).

::: HistoricalNote
- [SOR/2020-247, s. 8](#1274824-1286060){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1274824-1286060.html"}
:::

## [Coming into Force]{.HTitleText1} {#h-1004401 .Part}

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Coming into force

**[[27]{.sectionLabel}]{#
                            s-27 .sectionLabel}** These Guidelines come
into force on May 1, 1997.

::::::: section
:::::: Schedule
::: {}
# [SCHEDULE I]{.scheduleLabel}[(Subsection 2(1))]{.OriginatingRef}[Federal Child Support Tables]{.scheduleTitleText}  {#h-9 .scheduleLabel}
:::

*Notes:*

- ::::: listItemBlock0
  ::: listItemLabel
  [[1]{.lawlabel}]{#ScheduleProvision1ID0EBHA .lawLabel} 
  :::

  ::: listItemText2
  *The federal child support tables set out the amount of monthly child
  support payments for each province on the basis of the annual income
  of the spouse ordered to pay child support (the "support payer") and
  the number of children for whom a table amount is payable. Refer to
  these Guidelines to determine whether special measures apply.*
  :::
  :::::

- ::::: listItemBlock0
  ::: listItemLabel
  [[2]{.lawlabel}]{#ScheduleProvision2ID0EBGA .lawLabel} 
  :::

  ::: listItemText2
  *There is a threshold level of income below which no amount of child
  support is payable. The threshold is set at \$12,000. Child support
  amounts are specified for annual incomes up to \$150,000. For support
  payers with annual incomes over \$150,000, refer to section 4 of these
  Guidelines to determine the amount of child support.*
  :::
  :::::

- ::::: listItemBlock0
  ::: listItemLabel
  [[3]{.lawlabel}]{#ScheduleProvision3ID0ENFA .lawLabel} 
  :::

  ::: listItemText2
  *Income is set out in the tables in increments of \$1,000. Monthly
  amounts are determined by adding the applicable basic amount and the
  amount calculated by multiplying the applicable percentage by the
  portion of the income that exceeds the lower amount within that range
  of income.*
  :::
  :::::

  *Example:*

  *Province: British Columbia*

  *Number of children: 2*

  *Annual income of support payer: \$48,370*

  *Basic amount: \$752*

  *Percentage: 1.4%*

  *Lower amount of the income range: \$48,000*

  *The amount of monthly child support is calculated as follows:*

  *\$752 + \[1.4% × (\$48,370 - \$48,000)\]*

  *\$752 + \[1.4/100 × \$370\]*

  *\$752 + \[0.014 × \$370\]*

  *\$752 + \$5.18 = \$757.18*

- ::::: listItemBlock0
  ::: listItemLabel
  [[4]{.lawlabel}]{#ScheduleProvision4ID0EOEA .lawLabel} 
  :::

  ::: listItemText2
  *There are separate tables for each province. The amounts vary from
  one province to another because of differences in provincial income
  tax rates. The tables are in the following order:*
  :::
  :::::

  - [[(a)]{.lawlabel}]{#ScheduleProvision4Provision(a)ID0EBMEA
    .lawLabel} *Ontario;*

  - [[(b)]{.lawlabel}]{#ScheduleProvision4Provision(b)ID0EBLEA
    .lawLabel} *Quebec;*

  - [[(c)]{.lawlabel}]{#ScheduleProvision4Provision(c)ID0EBKEA
    .lawLabel} *Nova Scotia;*

  - [[(d)]{.lawlabel}]{#ScheduleProvision4Provision(d)ID0EBJEA
    .lawLabel} *New Brunswick;*

  - [[(e)]{.lawlabel}]{#ScheduleProvision4Provision(e)ID0EBIEA
    .lawLabel} *Manitoba;*

  - [[(f)]{.lawlabel}]{#ScheduleProvision4Provision(f)ID0EBHEA
    .lawLabel} *British Columbia;*

  - [[(g)]{.lawlabel}]{#ScheduleProvision4Provision(g)ID0EBGEA
    .lawLabel} *Prince Edward Island;*

  - [[(h)]{.lawlabel}]{#ScheduleProvision4Provision(h)ID0EBFEA
    .lawLabel} *Saskatchewan;*

  - [[(i)]{.lawlabel}]{#ScheduleProvision4Provision(i)ID0EBEEA
    .lawLabel} *Alberta;*

  - [[(j)]{.lawlabel}]{#ScheduleProvision4Provision(j)ID0EBDEA
    .lawLabel} *Newfoundland and Labrador;*

  - [[(k)]{.lawlabel}]{#ScheduleProvision4Provision(k)ID0EBCEA
    .lawLabel} *Yukon;*

  - [[(l)]{.lawlabel}]{#ScheduleProvision4Provision(l)ID0EBBEA
    .lawLabel} *Northwest Territories; and*

  - [[(m)]{.lawlabel}]{#ScheduleProvision4Provision(m)ID0EBAEA
    .lawLabel} *Nunavut.*

- ::::: listItemBlock0
  ::: listItemLabel
  [[5]{.lawlabel}]{#ScheduleProvision5ID0EBDA .lawLabel} 
  :::

  ::: listItemText2
  *The amounts in the tables are based on economic studies of average
  spending on children in families at different income levels in Canada.
  They are calculated on the basis that child support payments are no
  longer taxable in the hands of the receiving parent and no longer
  deductible by the paying parent. They are calculated using a
  mathematical formula and generated by a computer program.*
  :::
  :::::

- ::::: listItemBlock0
  ::: listItemLabel
  [[6]{.lawlabel}]{#ScheduleProvision6ID0EBCA .lawLabel} 
  :::

  ::: listItemText2
  *The formula referred to in note 5 sets support amounts to reflect
  average expenditures on children by a spouse with a particular number
  of children and level of income. The calculation is based on the
  support payer's income. The formula uses the basic personal amount for
  non-refundable tax credits to recognize personal expenses, and takes
  other federal and provincial income taxes and credits into account.
  Federal child tax benefits and the portion of the Goods and Services
  Tax/Harmonized Sales Tax credit that is attributable to children are
  excluded from the calculation. At lower income levels, the formula
  sets the amounts to take into account the combined impact of taxes and
  child support payments on the support payer's limited disposable
  income.*
  :::
  :::::

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/97-563, ss. 4 to 9;
- SOR/99-136, ss. 1, 2;
- SOR/2005-400, ss. 3 to 5;
- SOR/2011-267, s. 1;
- SOR/2017-224, ss. 1, 2.
:::

## [SCHEDULE II]{.scheduleLabel}[(Subsection 10(4))]{.OriginatingRef}[Comparison of Household Standards of Living Test]{.scheduleTitleText}  {#h-1004883 .scheduleLabel}
:::

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Definitions

  **1** The definitions in this section apply in this Schedule.

  [[average tax rate]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

  :   [[average tax rate]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}[\[Repealed,
      SOR/2000-337, s. 7\]]{.Repealed}

  [[child]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

  :   [[child]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means a child of the marriage or a
      child who

      - [(a)]{.lawlabel} is under the age of majority; or

      - [(b)]{.lawlabel} is the age of majority or over but is unable,
        by reason of illness, disability or other cause to obtain the
        necessaries of life. ([enfant]{.DefinedTermLink lang="fr"})

  [[household]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

  :   [[household]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means a spouse and any of the
      following persons residing with the spouse

      - [(a)]{.lawlabel} any person who has a legal duty to support the
        spouse or whom the spouse has a legal duty to support;

      - [(b)]{.lawlabel} any person who shares living expenses with the
        spouse or from whom the spouse otherwise receives an economic
        benefit as a result of living with that person, if the court
        considers it reasonable for that person to be considered part of
        the household; and

      - [(c)]{.lawlabel} any child whom the spouse or the person
        described in paragraph (a) or (b) has a legal duty to
        support. ([ménage]{.DefinedTermLink lang="fr"})

  [[taxable income]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

  :   [[taxable income]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means the annual taxable
      income determined using the calculations required to determine
      [[Taxable Income]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} in the T1 General form
      issued by the Canada Revenue Agency. ([revenu
      imposable]{.DefinedTermLink lang="fr"})

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Test

  **2** The comparison of household standards of living test is as
  follows:

  ***STEP 1***

  Establish the annual income of each person in each household by
  applying the formula

  ::: {#1004900 .Provision}
  A - B - C

  where

  [A]{.dfn}
  :   is the person's income determined in accordance with sections 15
      to 20 of these Guidelines,

  [B]{.dfn}
  :   is the federal and provincial taxes payable on the person's
      taxable income, and

  [C]{.dfn}
  :   is the person's source deductions for premiums paid under the
      [Employment Insurance Act](/eng/acts/E-5.6) and contributions made
      to the [Canada Pension Plan](/eng/acts/C-8) and the Quebec Pension
      Plan.
  :::

  Where the information on which to base the income determination is not
  provided, the court may impute income in the amount it considers
  appropriate.

  ***STEP 2***

  Adjust the annual income of each person in each household by

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} deducting the following amounts, calculated on an
    annual basis:

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} any amount relied on by the court as a factor
      that resulted in a determination of undue hardship, except any
      amount attributable to the support of a member of the household
      that is not incurred due to a disability or serious illness of
      that member,

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} the amount that would otherwise be payable by
      the person in respect of a child to whom the order relates, if the
      pleading of undue hardship was not made,

      - [(A)]{.lawlabel} under the applicable table, or

      - [(B)]{.lawlabel} as is considered by the court to be
        appropriate, where the court considers the table amount to be
        inappropriate,

    - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} any amount of support that is paid by the
      person under a judgment, order or written separation agreement,
      except

      - [(A)]{.lawlabel} an amount already deducted under subparagraph
        (i), and

      - [(B)]{.lawlabel} an amount paid by the person in respect of a
        child to whom the order referred to in subparagraph (ii)
        relates; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} adding the following amounts, calculated on an
    annual basis:

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} any amount that would otherwise be receivable by
      the person in respect of a child to whom the order relates, if the
      pleading of undue hardship was not made,

      - [(A)]{.lawlabel} under the applicable table, or

      - [(B)]{.lawlabel} as is considered by the court to be
        appropriate, where the court considers the table amount to be
        inappropriate,

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} any amount of child support that the person has
      received for any child under a judgment, order or written
      separation agreement.

  ***STEP 3***

  Add the amounts of adjusted annual income for all the persons in each
  household to determine the total household income for each household.

  ***STEP 4***

  Determine the applicable low-income measures amount for each household
  based on the following:

  <figure id="1004925">
  <table
  class="table table-hover table-striped tablePointsize8 topdouble topbot">
  <thead>
  <tr class="topdouble">
  <th class="noBorderRight borderBottom bottom" scope="col">Household
  Size</th>
  <th class="borderBottom bottom" scope="col">Low-income Measures
  Amount</th>
  </tr>
  </thead>
  <tbody>
  <tr>
  <td class="noBorderRight noBorderBottom top">One person</td>
  <td class="noBorderBottom top"></td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
  <td class="noBorderRight noBorderBottom">1 adult</td>
  <td class="noBorderBottom">$10,382</td>
  </tr>

  ***STEP 5***

  Divide the household income amount (Step 3) by the low-income measures
  amount (Step 4) to get a household income ratio for each household.

  ***STEP 6***

  Compare the household income ratios. The household that has the higher
  ratio has the higher standard of living.

## [SCHEDULE III]{.scheduleLabel}[(Section 16)]{.OriginatingRef}[Adjustments to Income]{.scheduleTitleText}  {#h-1004938 .scheduleLabel}
:::

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Employment expenses

  **1** Where the spouse is an employee, the spouse's applicable
  employment expenses described in the following provisions of the
  [Income Tax Act](/eng/acts/I-3.3) are deducted:

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} [\[Repealed, SOR/2000-337, s. 8\]]{.Repealed}

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} paragraph 8(1)(d) concerning expenses of teacher's
    exchange fund contribution;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} paragraph 8(1)(e) concerning expenses of railway
    employees;

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} paragraph 8(1)(f) concerning sales expenses;

  - [(e)]{.lawlabel} paragraph 8(1)(g) concerning transport employee's
    expenses;

  - [(f)]{.lawlabel} paragraph 8(1)(h) concerning travel expenses;

  - [(f.1)]{.lawlabel} paragraph 8(1)(h.1) concerning motor vehicle
    travel expenses;

  - [(g)]{.lawlabel} paragraph 8(1)(i) concerning dues and other
    expenses of performing duties;

  - [(h)]{.lawlabel} paragraph 8(l)(j) concerning motor vehicle and
    aircraft costs;

  - [(i)]{.lawlabel} paragraph 8(1)(l.1) concerning [Canada Pension
    Plan](/eng/acts/C-8) contributions and [Employment Insurance
    Act](/eng/acts/E-5.6) premiums paid in respect of another employee
    who acts as an assistant or substitute for the spouse;

  - [(j)]{.lawlabel} paragraph 8(1)(n) concerning salary reimbursement;

  - [(k)]{.lawlabel} paragraph 8(1)(o) concerning forfeited amounts;

  - [(l)]{.lawlabel} paragraph 8(1)(p) concerning musical instrument
    costs; and

  - [(m)]{.lawlabel} paragraph 8(1)(q) concerning artists' employment
    expenses.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Child support

  **2** Deduct any child support received that is included to determine
  total income in the T1 General form issued by the Canada Revenue
  Agency.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Spousal support and universal child
  care benefit

  **3** To calculate income for the purpose of determining an amount
  under an applicable table, deduct

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the spousal support received from the other spouse;
    and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} any universal child care benefit that is included
    to determine the spouse's total income in the T1 General form issued
    by the Canada Revenue Agency.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Special or extraordinary expenses

  **3.1** To calculate income for the purpose of determining an amount
  under section 7 of these Guidelines, deduct the spousal support paid
  to the other spouse and, as applicable, make the following adjustment
  in respect of universal child care benefits:

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} deduct benefits that are included to determine the
    spouse's total income in the T1 General form issued by the Canada
    Revenue Agency and that are for a child for whom special or
    extraordinary expenses are not being requested; or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} include benefits that are not included to determine
    the spouse's total income in the T1 General form issued by the
    Canada Revenue Agency and that are received by the spouse for a
    child for whom special or extraordinary expenses are being
    requested.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Social assistance

  **4** Deduct any amount of social assistance income that is not
  attributable to the spouse.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Dividends from taxable Canadian
  corporations

  **5** Replace the taxable amount of dividends from taxable Canadian
  corporations received by the spouse by the actual amount of those
  dividends received by the spouse.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Capital gains and capital losses

  **6** Replace the taxable capital gains realized in a year by the
  spouse by the actual amount of capital gains realized by the spouse in
  excess of the spouse's actual capital losses in that year.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Business investment losses

  **7** Deduct the actual amount of business investment losses suffered
  by the spouse during the year.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Carrying charges

  **8** Deduct the spouse's carrying charges and interest expenses that
  are paid by the spouse and that would be deductible under the [Income
  Tax Act](/eng/acts/I-3.3).

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Net self-employment income

  **9** Where the spouse's net self-employment income is determined by
  deducting an amount for salaries, benefits, wages or management fees,
  or other payments, paid to or on behalf of persons with whom the
  spouse does not deal at arm's length, include that amount, unless the
  spouse establishes that the payments were necessary to earn the
  self-employment income and were reasonable in the circumstances.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Additional amount

  **10** Where the spouse reports income from self-employment that, in
  accordance with sections 34.1 and 34.2 of the [Income Tax
  Act](/eng/acts/I-3.3), includes an additional amount earned in a prior
  period, deduct the amount earned in the prior period, net of reserves.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Capital cost allowance for property

  **11** Include the spouse's deduction for an allowable capital cost
  allowance with respect to real property.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Partnership or sole proprietorship
  income

  **12** Where the spouse earns income through a partnership or sole
  proprietorship, deduct any amount included in income that is properly
  required by the partnership or sole proprietorship for purposes of
  capitalization.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Employee stock options with a
  Canadian-controlled private corporation

  - **13** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Where the spouse has received, as an
    employee benefit, options to purchase shares of a
    Canadian-controlled private corporation, or a publicly traded
    corporation that is subject to the same tax treatment with reference
    to stock options as a Canadian-controlled private corporation, and
    has exercised those options during the year, add the difference
    between the value of the shares at the time the options are
    exercised and the amount paid by the spouse for the shares, and any
    amount paid by the   spouse to acquire the options to purchase the
    shares, to the income for the year in which the options are
    exercised.

  - [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Disposal of shares

    [(2)]{.lawlabel} If the spouse has disposed of the shares during a
    year, deduct from the income for that year the difference determined
    under subsection (1).

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Split-pension amount

  **14** If a spouse is deemed to have received a split-pension amount
  under paragraph 60.03(2)(b) of the [Income Tax Act](/eng/acts/I-3.3)
  that is included in that spouse's total income in the T1 General form
  issued by the Canada Revenue Agency, deduct that amount.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/97-563, ss. 12 to 14
- SOR/2000-337, ss. 8 to 11, 12(E)
- SOR/2001-292, s. 1
- SOR/2007-59, ss. 3, 4
- SOR/2009-181, s. 1

## AMENDMENTS NOT IN FORCE {#amendments-not-in-force .scheduleTitleText}

- --- SOR/2025-166, s. 1

  - [1]{.lawlabel} Note 3 of Schedule I to the [Federal Child Support
    Guidelines](/eng/regulations/SOR-97-175)[[Footnote
    ]{.wb-invisible}^1^](#fn_81000-2-3132-E_hq_20473){#fn_81000-2-3132-E_hq_20473-ID0EBCACAA}
    is replaced by the following:

    - ::: Footnote
      [[Return to footnote
      ]{.wb-invisible}^1^](#fn_81000-2-3132-E_hq_20473-ID0EBCACAA){#fn_81000-2-3132-E_hq_20473}SOR/97-175
      :::

    :::: section
    ::: AmendedText
    - ::::: listItemBlock0
      ::: listItemLabel
      [3]{.lawlabel} 
      :::

      ::: listItemText2
      *Income is set out in the tables in increments of \$1,000. Monthly
      amounts are determined by adding the applicable basic amount and
      the amount calculated by multiplying the applicable percentage by
      the portion of the income that exceeds the lower amount within
      that range of income.*
      :::
      :::::

      *Example:*

      *Province: British Columbia*

      *Number of children: 2*

      *Annual income of support payer: \$51,250*

      *Basic amount: \$807*

      *Percentage: 1.54%*

      *Lower amount of the income range: \$51,000*

      *The amount of monthly child support is calculated as follows:*

      *\$807 + \[1.54% × (\$51,250 - \$51,000)\]*

      *\$807 + \[1.54/100 × \$250\]*

      *\$807 + \[0.0154 × \$250\]*

      *\$807 + \$3.85 = \$810.85*
    :::
    ::::

- --- SOR/2025-166, s. 2

  - [2]{.lawlabel} The federal child support tables set out in Schedule
    I to the Guidelines are replaced by the federal child support tables
    set out in the schedule to these Guidelines.
